name: spring

attributes.attribute: a mythic site of fresh water with healing power
a thermal spring for cures in Roman times
a sign of richness and health

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: The spring is a mythic site. A well and a spring give the same water. They stand close in story. Both can heal. The power of the water works even across a distance. Water drawn from a well can help a sick body. Some springs give heat. The water comes out warm. The hot spring at Bath drew the sick in Roman times. The Celts tied water to yield, to growth, and to health in every region. A spring never ran dry, and the folk of the land counted on it as the year turned, from first frost to harvest.
